fact: Le Patriote reports that a connection failure in several arrondissement offices of Cotonou on Friday 11 September 2026 stopped the registering and validating of Droit Taxi payments, leaving motorcycle-taxi drivers waiting for hours; it gives no count of offices or drivers and names no provider.

Le Patriote states that Cotonou's arrondissement offices, sub-offices of the commune, register and validate Droit Taxi payments at the counter over a connection, such that its failure on 11 September 2026 blocked payment for the day; the payment system and its operator are not named.

Le Monde Local reports that the state agency ASIN presented at Bantè's town hall a project whose second axis is the connecting of the mairie to the Réseau National d'Administration (RNA), under the PRSCG 2 programme; the connection is presented as to come, not as made, and the session is undated, so the date is the article's.

Le Monde Local states that the planned connection of Bantè's mairie to the RNA is to allow smooth and secure communication with the central structures of the state; no system the staff would work in is named, and the date is the article's.

Le Monde Local names one commune, Bantè, as due to be connected to the RNA and calls it a pioneer commune under PRSCG 2, a programme it says is aimed at the local authorities of the Collines department; it gives no count of communes covered or connected, and the date is the article's.

Le Monde Local reports that the connection of Bantè's mairie to the RNA is led by a delegation of ASIN, the state's information systems agency, under the Programme de Renforcement des Structures Centrales de Gouvernance (PRSCG 2), with the prefect of the Collines overseeing; the date is the article's.
Le Monde Local places the connection of Bantè's mairie under the PRSCG 2 programme and states neither a cost nor who pays for it; the date is the article's.

Le Monde Local reports a working session at Bantè's town hall, chaired by the mayor with all heads of service, at which ASIN presented the connecting of the mairie to the RNA, more solar power and an official website; the session is undated, so the date is the article's.

Fraternité states that the holder of a cadastre registration certificate sells a parcel by going to the mairie as before, and that every operation is now done directly in e-Foncier Bénin, the national platform run by the state land agency ANDF; the connection the mairie works over is not described, and the date is the article's.
system: the mairies' working in e-Foncier Bénin

fact: Fraternité states that the national cadastre covers 24 arrondissements in 12 target communes with 445,695 parcels registered, and that the registration certificate is collected at the mairie in all 12; it gives no total of communes, and does not say how many mairies work in the platform themselves; the date is the article's.
system: the mairies' working in e-Foncier Bénin

fact: The Terra Bénin operations manual of 17 October 2025, written for the state land agency ANDF, assigns the mairie's land directorate (DADE) the receipt, checking, data entry, archiving and transmission to ANDF of land transaction files, and says communes, notaries and land offices keep the cadastre current by formalising transactions within e-Foncier Bénin; it sets the role out as procedure, and does not say how many mairies do it or over what connection.
system: the mairies' working in e-Foncier Bénin (e-FB)

fact: Fraternité reports that neighbourhood and village chiefs, who sit below the commune and its arrondissements, reach ANIP's platform for the residence-form code through their own mobile phones, with repeated failed attempts in Glo-Djigbé, Bohicon and Cotonou in March 2025; one chief's assistant suggests a terminal for each chief, which they do not have.
system: Chiefs' own mobile phones, used to reach ANIP's platform

fact: Fraternité reports that neighbourhood and village chiefs enter each residence-form request on ANIP's national platform to obtain a code, and that the platform often returns a service-unavailable message, some chiefs having issued no form at all by March 2025; the article blames the connection speed to ANIP's server.
system: Chiefs' own mobile phones, used to reach ANIP's platform

fact: The digital ministry's communications officer told La Nation that the electronic mail-management platform (Gec) had been deployed in several communes, naming Porto-Novo, Cotonou and Parakou with no count, and that unreliable internet connections and unsuitable equipment still hold it back; the article does not say whether the offices using it are the communes' own or how they are connected, and gives no date, so the publication date is used.
system: Connection used for the Gec platform in the communes

fact: La Nation reports that the national e-Foncier platform has been operational since 1 January 2025 with the active participation of town halls (mairies), notaries and surveyors, in a cadastre reform covering 12 communes and 32 arrondissements with 491,420 parcels registered, as presented by the land agency ANDF; the article does not say that town hall staff work in it from their own offices, nor how those offices are connected.
system: Connection used by town halls for the e-Foncier platform

fact: The digital ministry's portal states that the PRSCG programme aims to put in place a national network interconnecting 187 public-finance offices together with ministries, agencies, prefectures and town halls (mairies), and that most of the programme's infrastructure is already operational; dated to the article, 5 October 2021.

The digital ministry's portal names town halls (mairies) among the offices the PRSCG national network interconnects but gives no number of them, against a stated 187 public-finance offices; dated to the article, 5 October 2021.

The PRSCG is described as developed by the government of Benin, with its training run by the state agency ASSI under the supervision of the Ministry of Digital Affairs and Digitalisation, from 2 August to 17 September 2021.
The PRSCG is said to be developed by the government with the support of German technical cooperation; no budget line or amount is given; dated to the article, 5 October 2021.

Matin Libre reports that on 1 September 2026 the land-affairs directorate of Parakou's mairie presented 196,474 parcels registered in the national cadastre, citing figures from the e-Foncier Bénin platform, and showed a visiting Netherlands embassy delegation its working system for updating cadastral data; the article does not say how the office is connected.

Matin Libre names one commune, Parakou, whose mairie runs a system for updating its data in the national cadastre as of 1 September 2026; it gives no total of communes doing so, and beneficiaries ask for the project to continue in other communes.

The Ministry of Economy and Finance's 2025 SDG Eurobond report states that 12 new town halls used the services of the national administration network (RNA) in 2024; it is a count of additions in the year, with no cumulative total, beside the 77 communes the report gives for the country.
The report records 12 new town halls in 2024 as using the services of the state's national administration network, under the government's Administration intelligente project.

The report says the 12 new town halls of 2024 use 'the services' of the national administration network without naming them; the same table counts 12 new electronic mail-management (GEC) instances in 2024 at administrative structures, town halls and prefectures given as examples.

The report allocates EUR 6.43 million of the July 2021 EUR 500 million SDG Eurobond, a sovereign issue funding the public investment programme, to generalising e-services and digitalising the public administration, the line under which the 12 town halls joining the RNA in 2024 are reported.

The report names the Ministry of Digital Affairs (MND) as the ministry concerned for digital connectivity, with the state agency ASIN supplying tools to sector ministries; the RNA town-hall figure is reported under it.

KfW reports on 31 May 2023 that 187 authorities (ministries, the presidential office and prefectures) are connected in Benin's administrative network and that connecting all municipalities to it is the next step; no municipality is said to be on it.

KfW, on behalf of Germany's BMZ, financed the administrative network with EUR 10 million in a first phase, to which Benin's government added a counterpart of about EUR 4.8 million, and plans a further EUR 14.3 million in a second phase; connecting all municipalities is given as the next step.

The Government Action Programme 2021-2026 carries a project, Transformation numérique des collectivités locales, whose expected results include town halls and prefectures connected to the Administration's network, with the connection of communes to the network scheduled for 2023-2026 after studies in 2022; dated to the document's publication year.

The programme costs the local-government digital project at FCFA 21 billion, of which FCFA 7 billion from the national budget, FCFA 8 billion from public-private partnership and FCFA 6 billion from KfW; dated to the document's publication year.

The programme places the local-government digital project, including connection of town halls to the Administration's network, under the Ministry of Digital Affairs and Digitalisation, executed by the state agency ASSI; dated to the document's publication year.

The programme reports as done under the 2016-2021 programme a digital network dedicated to the public administration interconnecting 187 decentralised sites across the country, which it lists as tax collection offices, town halls, prefectures and others; it does not say how many of the 187 are town halls, and sets their connection as a result still expected for 2021-2026. Dated to the document's publication year.

The programme gives 187 sites on the Administration's network, town halls among several kinds of office listed, with no count of town halls or communes connected; dated to the document's publication year.
